metadata.title: Cooking with Kids: How to Make Sugar Cookie Pizzas from Scratch - Weelicious
metadata.description:
Sugar Cookie Pizza Recipe: http://bit.ly/SugarCookiePizzas  Are you looking for a really fun dessert idea to make with your kids? Sugar Cookie Pizzas! You'll love how simple, fast, and fun these cookie pizzas are to make. So will the kids! (of all ages) What kind of sugar cookie pizza did you make? Let us know! Post a comment below.

nodes.plm_action: Cut out some cookies.
nodes.plm_caption:
This video features a woman in an orange cardigan and a young child all together in the kitchen, making sugar cookies with frosting and fruit. The young child is sitting at the kitchen counter. The kitchen is well lit with natural lighting. The mother is teaching the child how to make the cookies.
The woman is holding a pale blue small bowl and the child presses the dough from the bowl onto a flat surface, then the two shape the dough into a circle using their hands. The mother lifts the cookie piece to show the camera, and both the woman and the child hold out cookie pieces. The woman holds a spoon over a container of whipped cream and honey, then pours the honey into a bowl, and the mother pours the cream into a bowl as well and stirs using the spoon. The child uses a knife to spread the cream over the cookies. The mother holds a flat yellow cookie in her hand, and the young child scoops out cream and puts it on top of the yellow cookie. The mother hands the cream knife to the child.
On the right side of the shot there is a small window with silver spoons, two bottles of cooking oil, a blender, and a paper roll. The woman is wearing a bright orange cardigan. The young child wears a black and white striped shirt. On the table are some colorful fruit, a big white plate, a bowl, and an orange sauce container.

summary.brief: A mother in an orange cardigan and her young child bake sugar‑cookie crusts, mix a cream‑cheese topping, and decorate the cookies with fruit.
summary.detailed: The video opens with title cards introducing the Sugar Cookie Pizza recipe. In a bright, sun‑lit kitchen the mother rolls out a batch of sugar‑cookie dough, presses it flat and uses a 5‑inch round cutter to form pizza‑shaped bases, which she places on parchment and bakes until cooked through. While the crusts bake, she combines cream cheese, honey and vanilla in a bowl and stirs until smooth. After the cookies cool, both mother and child spread the cream‑cheese mixture onto each crust, using a small knife or spoon. They then top the cookies with colorful fruit—blueberries for eyes, raspberries for noses, and slices of pear, apple, banana or similar fruits for mouths—to create smiley‑face designs. The finished sugar‑cookie pizzas are shown to the camera before the video ends with a website graphic.

action.detailed: Spread the cream‑cheese mixture onto each cookie crust and arrange fruit pieces to form smiley‑face decorations.
action.actor: the woman in the orange cardigan and her young child

nodes.plm_action: Hold up finished sugar cookie pizza
nodes.plm_caption:
The video is an advertisement for a recipe of Sugar Cookie Pizza.
The first shot is of a woman holding a baby in one hand and a sugar cookie in the other.
She smiles and interacts with the baby. At 2 seconds, the screen fades to orange and displays the words "Weelicious" and "Sugar Cookie Pizza."
In the next shot at 4 seconds, it shows two sugar cookies with a smiley face on the larger one and three dots to form the mouth on the smaller one.  The screen fades again.
The final shot is of two sugar cookies with frosting.

summary.brief: A woman in an orange cardigan cradles her baby while holding a sugar cookie, followed by animated title cards and images of decorated sugar‑cookie pizzas.
summary.detailed: The segment opens with a woman wearing an orange cardigan holding her baby on her hip and a round sugar cookie in her other hand, smiling and gently interacting with the child. The view then fades to an orange background that displays the Weelicious logo and the words “Sugar Cookie Pizza.” A subsequent graphic shows two sugar cookies—one larger cookie with a full smiley face and a smaller one with three dots forming a mouth. The segment ends with a still image of two frosted sugar‑cookie pizzas displayed together on a plate.

action.detailed: Hold the baby in one arm and raise the sugar cookie in the other hand while smiling at the child.
action.actor: A woman wearing an orange cardigan

nodes.plm_action: Make the cookies.
nodes.plm_caption:
The video shows a woman and a toddler baking cookies. There is a baking sheet and a table full of cookies. A woman explains and demonstrates how to make the cookies. There is a lot of talking going on in the video.
The video starts with a woman and a toddler standing at the counter. There is an empty counter space with a few things on it in the foreground, but the majority of the video takes place over the counter. A woman uses her hands and arms to hold things up for the toddler to set on the counter. The toddler has a blue bowl and a wooden spatula in front of them.
The woman grabs a spatula and a cookie and puts them into a large jar. She then goes to mix the ingredients in a large bowl with a spatula. She starts to grab the spatula and move it toward the toddler. The toddler goes over to the counter and starts picking up ingredients in her hand and puts it on top of the cookie.
The woman goes to mix some ingredients in another bowl. The toddler goes over to the counter and picks up a cookie and puts it on top of another cookie. The toddler then picks up a knife and she pushes it into a plate and uses it to spread something on the cookie. The toddler grabs a few more cookies from the counter and puts them in front of the bowl. The woman is holding up two cookies while talking to the camera. Then the toddler picks up one of the cookies and eats it and drops it.

summary.brief: A mother and her toddler roll, cut, bake sugar‑cookie circles, spread a sweet cream‑cheese topping, and decorate the cookies with fruit to make smiley‑face “pizza” treats.
summary.detailed: The woman in an orange cardigan and her toddler begin by flattening a sheet of sugar‑cookie dough and using a round cookie cutter to cut out individual crusts, which they place on parchment paper and bake in the oven for about 18–20 minutes. While the cookies cool, the woman mixes whipped cream cheese with honey and vanilla in a bowl until smooth. She then uses a knife to spread the creamy mixture onto each baked cookie crust. The toddler helps by scooping the cream and adding pieces of fruit—blueberries for eyes, a raspberry for a nose, and slices of pear, apple or banana for a mouth—to create happy‑face designs. The finished sugar‑cookie pizzas are held up to the camera at the end of the segment.

action.brief: Spread cream cheese topping and add fruit decorations
action.detailed: Spread the cream cheese mixture onto each baked cookie with a knife, then place blueberries, raspberries and other fruit pieces on top to form smiley‑face designs.
action.actor: the woman in the orange cardigan (the mother) together with her toddler

nodes.plm_action: Prepare the crust mixture.
nodes.plm_caption:
A well-lit video of a young girl and an adult preparing food on a kitchen counter top. The adult wears an orange cardigan, while the young girl wears a striped shirt. The person holding a knife, a rolling pin, a cup and a plate, and a tray on the table with the food items.  The young girl places a rolled piece of dough on the top of the plate, and is given a bottle of vanillae extract to add to the dough. She places the bottle on the table and stirs the contents into a bowl using a spoon. The adult then scoops out a small portion of the dough and places it onto the tray.  The adult scoops up some cream and places it into a small bowl, to which she then adds the child's vanillae extract.  Both the adult and the child are seen adding various fruits into the cream and placing it on the dough. They place the dough on another plate. The adult and child then place various fruits on the dough. The adult then holds up a smiley face made of the dough with fruit. The video is bright and well lit.
The only action is cooking.

summary.brief: A mother and her daughter roll, bake, and decorate sugar‑cookie pizzas.
summary.detailed: The woman in an orange cardigan rolls out the sugar‑cookie dough, presses a round cutter to form crusts and places them on a parchment‑lined sheet, then bakes them until cooked through. While the crusts bake, she mixes cream cheese, honey and vanilla in a bowl until smooth. After the cookies cool, she spreads the cream‑cheese frosting onto each crust with a knife while her daughter scoops and spreads the frosting with a small spoon. They then top the frosting with fresh fruit pieces—blueberries for eyes, a raspberry for a nose, and slices of pear or other fruit for a mouth—to create smiley‑face designs, and finish by stacking the decorated cookies like mini pizzas and showing the finished sugar‑cookie pizzas to the camera.

action.detailed: Roll out the dough, cut round crusts, bake them, mix cream cheese with honey and vanilla, spread the frosting onto each cooled crust, add fruit toppings to form smiley faces, and assemble the cookies as miniature pizzas.
action.actor: the mother in an orange cardigan (assisted by her young daughter)

summary_sent_to_llm.root_summary: The video opens with title cards introducing the Sugar Cookie Pizza recipe. In a bright, sun‑lit kitchen the mother rolls out a batch of sugar‑cookie dough, presses it flat and uses a 5‑inch round cutter to form pizza‑shaped bases, which she places on parchment and bakes until cooked through. While the crusts bake, she combines cream cheese, honey and vanilla in a bowl and stirs until smooth. After the cookies cool, both mother and child spread the cream‑cheese mixture onto each crust, using a small knife or spoon. They then top the cookies with colorful fruit—blueberries for eyes, raspberries for noses, and slices of pear, apple, banana or similar fruits for mouths—to create smiley‑face designs. The finished sugar‑cookie pizzas are shown to the camera before the video ends with a website graphic.

llm.system_prompt:
You evaluate YouTube videos for a video-understanding benchmark.

You will be given an Action100M-style summary of one video: title, description,
a hierarchical GPT-written summary of the whole video, and a deduplicated list
of action labels extracted at multiple levels of the video.

Your job is to judge:

1) DOMAINS — does this video clearly belong to either of these target domains?
   - "kitchen": a person preparing food in a kitchen-like setting
     (cooking, baking, food prep — NOT eating reviews, NOT pet-food prep,
     NOT food-product unboxing, NOT restaurant vlogs).
   - "manipulation": a person performing hand-object manipulation tasks
     with clear physical goals: assembly/disassembly, repair, crafting,
     tool use, packing, sorting. The video must show clear procedural
     manipulation, NOT just incidental hand movement (e.g. a vlog where
     someone holds things while talking does NOT count).
   A video can match neither, one, or both. Be strict — when in doubt,
   say "neither".

2) NUM_DISTINCT_EVENTS — count the number of *semantically distinct*
   sub-events (procedural steps) you see in the action list. Merge
   paraphrases of the same step into one. Ignore generic narration steps
   like "speak to camera" or "display title".

3) IS_GOOD_CANDIDATE — true only if BOTH:
   - at least one target domain matches
   - num_distinct_events > 3 (the video shows a real multi-step procedure)

Always return strict JSON in the requested schema.
